messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]

Date of Admission: [redacted]

Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted to the emergency department due to a 12-day history of cyclical fevers with vague abdominal pain.

Hospital Course:
Initial vital signs showed a blood pressure of 149/80 mmHg, a heart rate of 107 beats per minute, a temperature of 99.2ºF, a respiratory rate of 16, and a pulse oximetry reading of 100% on room air. Laboratory values showed a drop in hemoglobin and mild leukocytosis with no evidence of urinary tract infection. A computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast showed multiple liver abscesses, septic thrombophlebitis of the portal system, and evidence of ruptured appendicitis. The patient was started on broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and underwent IR-guided abscess drainage.

Treatment:
The patient was treated with IV antibiotics and underwent abscess drainage.

Condition at Discharge:
The patient's condition improved significantly after treatment.

Follow-Up:
Follow-up appointments were scheduled with the patient's primary care provider for further evaluation and treatment.

Restrictions:
The patient was advised to avoid strenuous activities until further notice.

Medications:
No medications were prescribed at the time of discharge.

Procedures:
The patient underwent IR-guided abscess drainage and interval appendectomy.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Summary:
The patient presented to the emergency department with a 12-day history of cyclical fevers with vague abdominal pain. Imaging studies revealed the presence of liver abscesses, septic thrombophlebitis of the portal system, and ruptured appendicitis. The patient was treated with IV antibiotics and underwent abscess drainage and interval appendectomy. The patient's condition improved significantly and follow-up appointments were scheduled with the primary care provider.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
**K75**

The main treatment this admission was IR-guided drainage of multiple liver abscesses (K75.0) with septic portal thrombophlebitis (K75.1). Both fall under category K75. This is a judgement call. If the coding rules require the underlying cause, ruptured appendicitis (K35), as principal, K35 would be the answer instead. I chose K75 because the abscesses were what was treated, and the appendectomy was an interval procedure that may not have happened in this admission.
